[PERSISTENT EXPERIENCE GUIDANCE]
## Consolidated Experience from Similar Tasks
Before acting, verify the environment and action validity instead of assuming success. Searches and finds can fail if the object does not exist or is not labeled as expected, so inspect available objects and known storage locations first. Moves can fail if the path is blocked, so check for obstacles and choose a clear route. Actions such as opening or manipulating can be invalid if the target or skill is unsupported, so confirm applicability and check feedback after each step. When the exact object is unavailable, adapt by searching for alternatives or valid labels. Always base the next step on observed results, not on predicted success.

## Preliminary Thinking
1) Inspect the scene for relevant objects and valid skills: potato, knife or cutting tool, pan or skillet, heat source or stove, and plate. 2) If the potato or required tools are not immediately visible, search known storage locations or explore available object instances; adapt to valid labels if an exact object is missing. 3) Verify that the cutting action is applicable and that no obstacle blocks access to the potato, then cut or obtain a potato slice. 4) Move carefully to the pan, heat source, and plate, checking that paths are clear and rerouting around obstacles like stools. 5) Verify the pan and heat source actions are valid, place the potato slice in the pan, and fry it using the appropriate cooking skill while monitoring feedback. 6) Once fried, move the potato slice to a plate using a valid serving or placing action. 7) Confirm each action succeeded before proceeding; if any action fails, inspect the error and try an alternative valid object, location, or skill.
[/PERSISTENT EXPERIENCE GUIDANCE]
